title: High-resolution immunofluorescence imaging of mouse cochlear hair bundles
protocol: Euthanize the mouse following laboratory animal care procedures.
Decapitate the euthanized mouse.
Remove the skin of the head by cutting from the posterior, caudal base of the skull toward the rostral part of the skull using dissection scissors.
Hemisect the skull along the sagittal plane with dissection scissors or a scalpel.
Remove the brain from the hemisected skull.
Extract the portion of the skull containing the inner ear.
Transfer the skull portion to a dissection dish containing dissection medium.
Extract the inner ear from the surrounding bone.
Remove the stapes from the oval window if still present.
Transfer the inner ear to a plate containing 4% PFA fixative using a small spoon.
Make a hole at the apex of the cochlea.
Perfuse fixative through the round and oval windows using a needle and syringe.
Incubate the cochlea in fixative for 30 minutes.
Transfer the incubated cochlea to PBS.
Remove the portion of the temporal bone containing the cochlea and vestibule from the skull.
Place the bone with the cochlea and vestibule into dissection buffer at 25°C.
Gently detach the outer edges of the cochlea and vestibule using #5 forceps.
Trim away additional tissue around the cochlea and remove the stapes if still attached.
Transfer the cochlea to a dish containing 4% PFA diluted in dissection buffer at 25°C.
Open a small hole in the apex of the cochlea.
Gently flush 0.5 ml fixative through the oval window using a 1-mL syringe with a 26G × ½ needle.
Flush 0.5 ml fixative through the round window using a 1-mL syringe with a 26G × ½ needle.
Transfer the cochlea to a 2-ml tube containing 1.5 ml of fixative using a small spoon.
Incubate the cochlea in fixative at 25°C for 30 min.
Transfer the fixed cochlea to a 2-ml tube containing 1.5 ml of PBS using a spoon.
Place the inner ear in a dish containing PBS.
Chip away the cochlear bone starting from the apex and working toward the base.
Gently remove the outer bone along the cochlear length with #5 forceps starting from the hole at the apex of the cochlea.
Crack along the center of the spirals, avoiding areas where the stria abuts the bone.
Chip away remaining bone to reveal the stria vascularis once a hole has been opened along the cochlea.
Grip the vestibule with forceps if it is still connected to the cochlea to restrain the organ for dissection.
Slowly remove the stria vascularis starting from the apical point using fine #55 forceps.
For P6 and younger mice, often the whole stria can be removed in one attempt, spiraling down the organ.
Remove Reissner’s membrane using #55 forceps.
Remove the tectorial membrane using #55 forceps.
Gently grab the tectorial membrane above the hair cells with fine (#55) forceps.
Pull the tectorial membrane away from the tissue to make it visible and unroll.
Puncture or tear the tissue between the organ of Corti and the modiolus using forceps.
Release the organ of Corti from the modiolus.
Permeabilize the tissue to open pores in the membrane.
Block the tissue to prevent nonspecific antibody binding.
Incubate the tissue with primary antibody targeting the protein of interest.
Incubate the tissue with secondary antibody providing immunofluorescence to the target of interest.
Incubate the sample with phalloidin to stain actin filaments of the stereociliary cytoskeleton.
Mount the sample for ease of imaging.
Transfer the organ of Corti to a glass Micro-Test Staining Dish containing 200 μL permeabilization buffer (4% BSA in PBS with 0.05% Triton X-100).
Remove the permeabilization buffer, keeping a small drop to cover the tissue.
Add permeabilization buffer for 20 min at 25°C, shaking.
Remove the permeabilization buffer and add blocking buffer for 1 h at 25°C, shaking.
Discard the blocking buffer and incubate the tissue with diluted primary antibodies in buffer for 12–16 h at 4°C, shaking.
Remove the primary antibody solution and wash the tissue with blocking buffer three times for 5 min each at 25°C, shaking.
Add buffer containing diluted fluorescent secondary antibodies for 1 hour at 25°C, shaking.
Discard the secondary antibody solution.
Wash tissue with blocking buffer once for 5 minutes at 25°C, shaking.
Remove blocking buffer.
Add buffer containing diluted fluorescently labeled phalloidin for 20 minutes at 25°C, shaking.
Remove the blocking buffer, leaving a small drop of solution covering the sample.
Add 200 μL of dilution buffer (1% BSA in PBS with 0.05% Tween-20) containing the diluted primary antibody.
Incubate at 4°C for 12–16 hours with gentle shaking.
Place the sample plate in a Western blot box or empty pipette tip box with a lid to prevent liquid evaporation during longer incubations.
Saturate the air in the box with water and further limit evaporation by placing a Kimwipe dampened with distilled water in the bottom of the box below the Micro-Test Staining Dish.
Seal the box with parafilm.
Remove the primary antibody solution, leaving a small drop covering the sample.
Wash 3 × 5 minutes with 200 μL dilution buffer at 25°C with gentle shaking.
Remove the dilution buffer, leaving a small drop covering the sample.
Add 200 μL of dilution buffer (1% BSA in PBS with 0.05% Tween-20) containing the diluted secondary antibody.
Incubate at 25°C for 1 hour, protected from light, with gentle shaking.
Wash 1 × 5 minutes with dilution buffer at 25°C with gentle shaking.
Remove the dilution buffer, leaving a small drop covering the sample.
Add 200 μL of dilution buffer (1% BSA in PBS with 0.05% Tween-20) with diluted phalloidin (1:500 or 1:1000 dilution).
Incubate at 25°C for 20 minutes, protected from light, with gentle shaking.
Wash 5 × 5 minutes with dilution buffer at 25°C with gentle shaking.
Remove any remaining pieces of Reissner’s membrane if still attached.
Cut the tissue into “turns” that can lie flat on the slide without overlapping.
Transfer the turn to the slide using a small spoon.
Remove excess liquid with a pipette, leaving a small drop of liquid covering the tissue.
Add a drop of mounting medium on top of the tissue.
Orient the tissue with the hair bundles facing upward.
Place one edge of the coverslip against the slide.
Gently roll the coverslip onto the turn in the direction of sound-induced force deflection and hold firmly for 10 seconds.
Absorb any excess mounting medium with a Kimwipe.
Seal the coverslip in place with fingernail polish to prevent movement while the mounting medium is hardening.
Transfer the turns of the organ of Corti to the slide using a small spoon or an enlarged glass Pasteur pipette tip.
Remove excess liquid with a pipette but keep a small drop to cover the tissue.
Add a drop of mounting medium onto the turn.
Remove as much dilution buffer as possible from the turn.
Place the turn in the mounting medium to avoid air contact.
Orient the sample facing upward under the stereomicroscope using forceps.
Push the sample to the bottom of the mounting medium droplet until it sits on the glass slide.
Ensure the turn is facing upward when mounting.
Select a large region of hair bundles.
Slowly roll the coverslip down onto the sample in the direction that the hair bundles would be deflected by sound-induced forces.
Hold the coverslip firmly in place for 10 seconds.
Remove excess mounting medium from the edges of the coverslip with a Kimwipe.
Seal the coverslip with nail polish if appropriate.
Use a confocal microscope to localize fluorescently labeled proteins within the stereocilia in samples mounted below a coverslip.
Locate and bring the turn into focus using the phalloidin emission channel under 10× magnification.
Switch to at least a 63× objective for detailed imaging.
Add proper immersion medium for the objective (e.g., oil, glycerol).
Visually scan the sample to identify regions with hair bundles properly oriented for imaging.
Center the region of interest and switch to acquisition mode.
Adjust laser intensity and gain in the phalloidin channel such that no pixels are oversaturated.
Adjust laser intensity and gain for the protein of interest channel such that no pixels are oversaturated.
Select the z-stack region and step size.
Crop the image to the bundles of interest.
Set the pinhole size, averaging, accumulation, and speed of acquisition to obtain optimal images.
Acquire the image z-stack.
Adjust image parameters post-imaging using an image processing software.
Select a z-slice containing the staining of interest.
Generate a maximum intensity projection by selecting a range of z-slices.
Create a 3D-reconstruction of the image to localize the protein of interest.
